notes: Modelling study of CO2 mineralization rate of prototypical slags vs grinding; no experiments on specific slag samples.

1 Scientific Literature.Title: Enhancing CO2 Mineralization Rate and Extent of Iron and Steel Slag via Grinding
1 Scientific Literature.Authors: Corey Myers, Jun Sasagawa, Takao Nakagaki
1 Scientific Literature.Study_Objective: Use an experimentally verified diffusion/reaction model to assess how crystallinity, grain size, RH, CO2 concentration and temperature accelerate CO2 mineralization of iron and steel slags, and the energy penalty.
1 Scientific Literature.Abstract_or_Key_Finding: Crystallinity, high RH and grinding (to ~1-10 um, avoiding amorphization) give largest rate gains at lowest energy; ~1000x acceleration at ~100 MJ/t-CO2 theoretically, ~500 MJ/t-CO2 practically. Raising CO2 concentration or temperature gives only modest gains at high energy cost. BOF/EAF slag with standard PSD mineralize nearly fully within a few days. For BF slag, CO2 mineralization beats ggbs sale above 67.40 USD/t-CO2.
